text: This week's mistake: skipping the soil test to save money.
Your foundation sits on the soil, and the soil decides how it should be designed.
Some soils are firm. Some, like black cotton soil, swell when wet and shrink when dry.
Design the foundation without knowing, and it can end up too weak, or costlier than it needs to be.
And cracks that show up years later are much harder to fix.
So before your foundation is designed, ask your engineer: do we need a soil test here, and what will it tell us?
A small step, before the biggest part of your house.
Save this before you start digging.
